newsitem.title: FINLAND: Sisu Oy says Renault may buy lorry ops.
newsitem.headline: Sisu Oy says Renault may buy lorry ops.

text.p: Finnish state-owned vehicle maker Sisu Oy said at the weekend it was possible that French carmaker Renault would buy its lorry business.
"The negotiations are still going on, but I cannot exclude that possibility," managing director Christer Granskog told Finnish television news in an interview broadcast on Sunday.

In June, Sisu and Renault signed a letter of intent to establish a 50-50 joint venture to handle sales and servicing of all Sisu and Renault lorries in Finland, the Baltic states and nearby regions of Russia.
The joint venture's annual net sales would be about 650 million markka ($140 million), Sisu said in June.
In 1995, Sisu's lorry business had net sales of 700 million markka, or 11 percent of Sisu's consolidated net sales. The unit reported an operating profit of five million markka.
In its January-August 1996 interim report, Sisu did not give a net sales figure for Sisu Trucks, but said it was unprofitable.

Granskog also told the TV news he hoped Sisu might be partly privatised and listed on the Helsinki Stock Exchange, maybe in 1997. The state owns 73.6 percent of Sisu and has been authorised by parliament to cut the stake to 50 percent.
